newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: China says Spratlys incursion legal, normal.
newsitem.headline: China says Spratlys incursion legal, normal.

text.p: The Chinese embassy in Manila said on Saturday the presence of Chinese armed naval ships in the disputed Spratly islands in the South China Sea was legal and normal.

"It is China's proper legal rights and is unobjectionable that China conducted normal activities of peaceful use within the water of its own jurisdiction," embassy spokesman Hao Yinbiao said in a statement.
Hao said the ships, armed with deck guns, were conducting only marine survey measurements in the area and had returned to China upon completion of the survey.
The Philippines protested against the presence of the ships in the vicinity of two islands it is claiming.

A diplomatic note was sent to the Chinese embassy on April 30 saying it had violated a code of conduct between the two countries requiring both sides not to take any action that would disturb peace in the area.
The Spratlys are a cluster of isles, reefs and shoals believed to be potentially rich in oil and gas.
Beijing says the entire area historically belongs to China. The islands are also claimed wholly or in part by Vietnam, Taiwan, the Philippines, Malaysia and Brunei.
